## Results of the suite on a CPU build and a CUDA build (`-DCUDA`) {#sec-ch13-results}

### Summary

This section records what the whole suite gives at the code pin. The reference result is the project's own
continuous integration, which installs every test dependency and passes all 49 `ctest` entries on Linux and macOS,
on CPU. A CUDA build has no such reference, because the integration runners have no GPU, so the CUDA counts here come
from a recorded run on one GPU host. That host run also shows how one entry fails when a test dependency is missing,
so a reader can tell such an environment failure from a real regression.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Pass, fail and skip counts of the suite at the pin.

**Data.** The project integration (49 of 49, CPU); a recorded CPU and CUDA host run.

**Placement.** After the build and install; see @sec-ch13-suite.

**Activation.** `cmake -B build -DCUDA=OFF` or `-DCUDA=ON`; the build itself is described in @sec-ch12.

**Guarantee / limits.** 49 of 49 with all test dependencies; missing ones fail one entry.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme records measurements.

### Numerical method

No numerical method. The reference run is the integration workflow {{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml >}}. It
installs `pytest` and `setuptools-scm` with the other Python dependencies, builds and installs kintera, and runs
`ctest --output-on-failure` in the build's test directory, on a Linux and a macOS runner.

The host runs used two Release builds of the pin, one with `-DCUDA=OFF` and one with `-DCUDA=ON`, installed into a
private directory with `pip install . --no-build-isolation --no-deps --target <dir>`. That host's Python environment
had no `setuptools-scm`, and its file system refuses symbolic links. Each build was tested in two ways:

1. a serial `ctest` run in `build/tests`, with the test inputs copied into that directory (@sec-ch13-suite, Limits);
2. one `pytest` run over the whole `tests/` directory from the source tree, against the installed build.

The CPU build was tested with no GPU visible, so its CUDA cases skip instead of failing on a build without CUDA
kernels.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| all 49 entries, integration (Linux, macOS) | the suite passes | exact counts | the `ctest` summary |
| all 49 entries, host CPU and CUDA builds | the suite passes | exact counts | the `ctest` summary |

: Suite runs at the pin. {#tbl-ch13-results-tests}

The reference result: the project integration at the pin passes 49 of 49 `ctest` entries on both its Linux and its
macOS runner, including `test_version_floor.py` and `test_version_fallback.py`, with `setuptools-scm`
10.3.4 installed.[^ch13-results-ci]

The host runs reproduce everything except the version tests, for the environmental reasons given below. On the host
CPU build, serial `ctest` passes 48 of 49 entries. `pytest` over `tests/` gives 412 passed, 174 skipped and
0 failed.[^ch13-results-cpu] Almost all of the 174 skips are CUDA cases with no GPU visible. The others are:

- 4 cases of `test_atm2d.py`, which need the CUDA sparse solver;
- 4 cases of `test_kinetics_base.py`, which need external data (@sec-ch13-kinetics-base);
- the module `test_version_floor.py`.

On the CUDA build, serial `ctest` passes 48 of 49 entries. `pytest` gives 584 passed, 6 skipped and 0
failed.[^ch13-results-cuda] The 6 skips are the 4 external-data cases of `test_kinetics_base.py` and the two version
modules. The C++ programs pass with 105 CUDA instances and 105 CPU instances passing and none failing; the device
dispatch behind those instances is described in @sec-ch12.

The one failing `ctest` entry on both host builds is `test_version_floor.py`. It fails because the host lacks a test
dependency that the integration installs; it is not a defect of the code. The
module calls `pytest.importorskip("setuptools_scm")` at import, before any test is defined
({{< code tests/test_version_floor.py >}}). Without that package, `pytest` collects no test, reports `1 skipped`, and
exits with code 5, "no tests collected". `ctest` counts any non-zero exit as a failure. The sibling
`test_version_fallback.py` makes the same check inside its test function
`test_archive_version_is_not_older_than_the_newest_release`
({{< code tests/test_version_fallback.py test_archive_version_is_not_older_than_the_newest_release >}}). The test is
collected and skipped, `pytest` exits 0, and that entry passes.[^ch13-results-exit5] With `setuptools_scm` present,
the version tests run. On a file system that refuses symbolic links they then fail for another environmental reason:
`tar -x` cannot recreate the repository's symbolic links in the test's archive.[^ch13-results-tar]

### Limits

- The CUDA counts are for one host type (compute capability 6.1 GPUs, CUDA 12.6) and one set of library versions.
  No integration run covers CUDA.
- A host without `setuptools-scm`, or with a file system that refuses symbolic links, fails the version tests: 48 of
  49 is the expected `ctest` result there, not a regression.
- TODO: run times per entry; not measured.
